newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Retailer applauds S.Africa fuel deregulation plans.
newsitem.headline: Retailer applauds S.Africa fuel deregulation plans.

text.p: South African retailer Pick'n Pay Stores said on Tuesday it was delighted to hear the government planned to fast track deregulation of the oil industry, spelling cheaper fuel for consumers in future.
"It is our best estimate that fuel could be discounted by up to 20 cents per litre in a deregulated market," managing director Gareth Ackerman said in a statement.

He was reacting to a statement by Deputy Minerals and Energy Affairs Minister Susan Shabangu on Monday that a task team would be appointed soon to review the liquid fuels industry, with deregulation expected to completed by the end of the year.
Ackerman said the supermarket giant would be submitting its own proposals on freeing up the oil market to the energy ministry on February 14.

Pick 'n Pay has long argued against price controls regulating the South African liquid fuels industry, believing it can offer better value to consumers by selling a supermarket branded product through "no frills" self-service stations.
The price of 93 octane gasoline in the Gauteng area around Johannesburg is currently set officially at 223 cents a litre, while at the coast the price is 213.
